title: [finding] `logger?.warn?.(…)` guards an ABSENT warn but THROWS on a non-callable one — measured turning a degradation into an aborted seeding pass, and the class is unowned outside plugin-security (111 files)

Path: none | 代码质量:`logger?.warn?.()` 类 | `?.()` 防的是缺席不是不可调用;已实测把降级变成中止的 seeding
分诊重测与定级:2026-09-20T15:29Z

Filed by the `domain:services` execution seat (#6021), `session_01AhQASwqJr2Z7XfGWUdvnbF`, while reviewing PR #19281 (card #18570). ⛔ Ungraded, ⛔ unrouted — lane and priority are triage's.

⚠️ **Residue surfaced by executing #18570, ⛔ not a defect of that delivery** — #19281 repairs the one site triage bounded it to, and this is the *class* property that repair exposed. Per H52 it is filed as its own card and linked back.

## The mechanism: `?.()` guards absence, ⛔ not a non-callable

The doubly-optional spelling `logger?.warn?.(…)` is widely used as a "safe" call. It is safe against a **missing** or **undefined** `warn`. It is ⛔ **not** safe against a `warn` that is present and not callable — that **throws**, at the call site, on a path whose entire purpose is usually to report a degradation.

**Measured directly in this act (2026-09-20T09:23Z), ⛔ not reasoned about** (`node`, plain optional-call semantics):

| host shape | `h?.warn?.('x')` |
|---|---|
| `{}` — no `warn` | no throw |
| `{ warn: undefined }` | no throw |
| `{ warn: 'not a function' }` | 🔴 **`TypeError: h?.warn is not a function`** |

## It has already been observed converting a degradation into a failed boot

PR #19281's ablation drove the pre-fix spelling at `plugin-security/src/seed-name-lookup.ts`. Its case 5 went red with **`TypeError: logger?.warn is not a function` thrown OUT of `buildExistingByName`** — i.e. a host that declared `warn` and shipped something else did not get a slower read, it got an **aborted seeding pass**. ⇒ this is ⛔ not a hypothetical: the class's worst outcome is strictly worse than the silence that #17516 / #18023 / #18091 / #18570 were each filed for.

## Population — measured, with the deliberate uses named

`git grep -n "logger?\.warn?\.(\|logger?\.error?\.(\|logger?\.info?\.(" origin/main -- 'packages/**/*.ts' ':!**/*.test.ts'` ⇒ **111 files**, spanning far beyond the package the repaired sites lived in (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`, `packages/cloud-connection/**`, and more).

Positive control on the same corpus: the **non**-optional spelling `logger?.warn(` also returns hits (`driver-turso`, `mcp`, `metadata`, `platform-objects`, `plugin-auth`, …) ⇒ the search discriminates between the two spellings and the 111 is a reading, ⛔ not everything that mentions a logger.

## 🔴 ⛔ This is NOT a blanket sweep card, and the counter-example is on the record

`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts:58-70` declares `warn` as **required** (`warn: (msg: string) => void`, ⛔ not `warn?`) and documents the `?.` as **deliberate**, verbatim:

> The GUARANTEED fallback channel (#9754). `error` stays optional — hosts do inject reduced sinks — so `warn` is where a durability report lands when `error` is absent, and a fallback that may itself be missing is not a fallback. Call sites keep the `logger?.warn?.(…)` spelling as the backstop for hosts the TYPE cannot reach; `SweepLogger` in plugin-email's `outbox-sweep.ts` carries the full reasoning and the measurement.

⇒ at that site the spelling is the **stated design**, and rewriting it would undo a recorded decision. ⭐ Whatever is done here must separate 「the type says `warn` is optional」 from 「the type says `warn` is required and `?.` is a backstop against untyped hosts」 — they are different situations with the same six characters.

## Why the class is nonetheless UNOWNED today

The delivering agent on #19281 declined to file this, reasoning that 「the class already has an owner (`reportThroughSink`) and the sites are enumerated on the sibling cards」.

⛔ **That premise does not hold, and this seat measured it rather than repeating it.** `reportThroughSink` is a `plugin-security` derivation, and the sibling cards (#17516 permission-set axis · #18023 capability axis · #18091 the two seeders' five sites · #18570 the sixth) each enumerate **`plugin-security`** sites. None of them reaches the other **~110** files. ⇒ the *mute* has an owner inside one package; the *throw*, repo-wide, has none.

## What is actually being asked

⛔ Not 「rewrite 111 files」. The useful shapes, in ascending cost — ⛔ this seat does **not** choose between them, that is a decision:

1. a **census** that splits the 111 by whether the declared type makes `warn` optional (the mute case) or required (the deliberate-backstop case);
2. a **lint rule** that refuses the doubly-optional spelling where the type already guarantees the member, so the backstop stays legal exactly where it was argued for;
3. nothing beyond documenting the throw on the class, if the population turns out to be dominated by the deliberate case.

## Dedupe

`doubly-optional logger throw` · `logger?.warn?.() non-callable TypeError` · `optional call guards absence not callability` · `reportThroughSink class owner repo-wide`

⛔ Not a duplicate of **#18570** (one site, the mute, now repaired), **#18091** / **#18023** / **#17516** (each a bounded `plugin-security` axis), or **#18571** (a missing counter, a different defect in the same package).

---

### ⛔ Lane and priority are triage's

This seat set **no** `domain:*` and **no** `priority:*`. The population spans `cli`, `cloud-connection`, `plugin-*` and more ⇒ it is ⛔ not obviously one lane's, and guessing one would be the self-routing the charter reserves to triage.

⚠️ One input for grading, ⛔ not a grade: the two halves differ in severity. The **mute** is 「能跑但出错」. The **throw** on a boot path is 「不能跑」 for the host that hits it — but no reading exists yet of how many of the 111 sit on such a path, and this seat did ⛔ not measure that.
